summary: Opt-in committed smallclaims view invalidations with bounded journals and cursor gaps

replay.detail: Event installation is explicit and starts at current frontiers without scanning history. No GET/open/migration backfill or asynchronous catch-up is enabled.

schema.detail: Explicit events::install creates three local derived tables, indexes and invalidation triggers in an already opt-in IVM store. Existing daemon stores/runtimes create none of them. No production schema/rules version bump or automatic migration.

rules.detail: Replicated claim order, admission rules and checkpoint rules remain unchanged. No production checkpoint participation or retention policy is added.

compatibility.detail: Adds Rust library feed and publisher APIs, without a daemon wire or consumer switch. The reference ViewRuntime now rejects ReplaceOriginal registrations until repair-before-projection eligibility is proved; RetainOriginal remains supported. Storage errors propagate instead of persisting an operator fence.

downtime.detail: No service restart or production activation. Commit-inclusive writer cost and production source coverage remain adoption gates.

manual.detail: Library adopters explicitly install the event feed and attach a Publisher after certifying source coverage. Follow IVM_EVENTS.md; graph-watch owns transport and client authority. Restore/clone owners must explicitly rotate database identity before exposing the file.

recovery.detail: Rollback/reopen controls cover local event state; production checkpoint/restore/cross-runtime recovery is not certified. Expired or replaced cursors require explicit resync, and missing/oversized feed evidence cannot silently become ready.
